name: Ketonemia Classification Rules
purpose: Deterministic, reviewable rule set that runs the Classification Protocol. Maps structured context inputs to governed reference output: KSO class, KSS language, boundary statement, canonical references, and source requirements.
governing_rule: This engine classifies the interpretive frame around a blood ketone signal. It does not classify a person, diagnose a condition, triage urgency, recommend treatment, or declare safety or danger.
matching: First rule in this array whose 'when' conditions all match the selected inputs wins. Fields omitted from 'when' are wildcards. The final rule is an unconditional catch-all so the engine never fails to produce a governed output.
constant_boundary_statement: This classification does not diagnose, triage, declare safety, or interpret an individual reading.
sensitive_boundary_statement: This belongs near the clinical-boundary layer. Ketonemia.com can explain terminology and source pathways, but it cannot assess a person, determine urgency, diagnose DKA, or provide instructions.
